name: MonarchDataTable
title: DataTable
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyColumn with a header row, sized by androidx.compose.foundation.layout.BoxWithConstraints; androidx.compose.material3.Checkbox and TriStateCheckbox for selection; androidx.compose.material3.DropdownMenu for row actions and the sort menu; MonarchSkeleton, MonarchEmptyState and MonarchErrorState for the states
summary: Records in columns: a table on wide screens and a list of records with a labelled line per field on phones, with sorting, selection, row actions, column visibility and order, and the loading, empty, filtered and error states. Read-only.
whenToUse: For a set of records the person scans, sorts, selects and acts on: tickets, invoices, contacts, users.
whenNotToUse: For editable cells there is no Monarch component yet; open a form instead. For a short list of things use a LazyColumn of rows such as MonarchInboxRow. For key and value pairs of one record use MonarchDescriptionList.
api: @Composable public fun <T, K : Any> MonarchDataTable(caption: String, rows: List<T>, columns: List<MonarchDataTableColumn<T>>, rowKey: (T) -> K, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, sort: MonarchDataTableSort? = null, onSortChange: ((MonarchDataTableSort) -> Unit)? = null, selection: Set<K>? = null, onSelectionChange: ((Set<K>) -> Unit)? = null, hiddenColumns: Set<String> = emptySet(), columnOrder: List<String> = emptyList(), layout: MonarchDataTableLayout = MonarchDataTableLayout.Automatic, sortsRows: Boolean = true, loading: Boolean = false, errorMessage: String? = null, filtered: Boolean = false, rowLabel: ((T) -> String)? = null, rowSelectable: (T) -> Boolean = { true }, rowActions: ((T) -> List<MonarchDataTableRowAction>)? = null, onRetry: (() -> Unit)? = null, onClearFilters: (() -> Unit)? = null, onOpen: ((T) -> Unit)? = null, actionsIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, state: LazyListState = rememberLazyListState(), labels: MonarchDataTableLabels = MonarchDataTableLabels(), footer: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null)

public class MonarchDataTableColumn<T>(title: String, id: String = title, numeric: Boolean = false, sortable: Boolean = true, hideable: Boolean = true, weight: Float = 1f, comparator: Comparator<T>? = null, value: (T) -> String) { val chooserColumn: MonarchColumnChooserColumn }
public class MonarchDataTableSort(columnId: String, direction: MonarchDataTableSortDirection = MonarchDataTableSortDirection.Ascending) { fun toggled(): MonarchDataTableSort }
public enum class MonarchDataTableSortDirection { Ascending, Descending }
public class MonarchDataTableRowAction(title: String, id: String = title, danger: Boolean = false, enabled: Boolean = true, onClick: () -> Unit)
public enum class MonarchDataTableLayout { Automatic, Table, List }

public class MonarchDataTableLabels(selectAll: String? = null, selectRow: ((row: String) -> String)? = null, selectedCount: ((count: Int) -> String)? = null, rowActions: ((row: String) -> String)? = null, actionsText: String? = null, open: String? = null, sort: String? = null, sortedAscending: String? = null, sortedDescending: String? = null, notSorted: String? = null, noValue: String? = null, loading: String? = null, emptyTitle: String? = null, emptyMessage: String? = null, filteredTitle: String? = null, filteredMessage: String? = null, errorTitle: String? = null)

options.name: caption
options.description: Names the table for TalkBack, such as "Open tickets".

options.name: rows
options.description: The rows, in the app's order.

options.name: columns
options.description: Every column in its default order: header, cell text, numeric alignment, sort rule, whether it sorts and hides, width share.

options.name: rowKey
options.description: A row's stable, unique key, also the key in selection and the lazy key; use a String, Int or Long.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the table. The table scrolls itself; bound its height inside a scrolling parent.

options.name: sort
options.description: The sort, one column and a direction, or null for the app's order.

options.name: onSortChange
options.description: Receives the new sort from a header or the Sort menu. Without it nothing sorts.

options.name: selection
options.description: The selected keys. With onSelectionChange, rows get checkboxes and a select-all checkbox appears above them.

options.name: onSelectionChange
options.description: Receives the whole new selection.

options.name: hiddenColumns
options.description: Ids of hidden columns, as MonarchColumnChooser writes them. Columns that are not hideable stay shown.

options.name: columnOrder
options.description: Column ids in display order; missing ids follow in their default order.

options.name: layout
options.description: A table from 640dp of width below font scale 1.5 and a list of records otherwise, or always one of them.

options.name: sortsRows
options.description: Whether the table sorts rows itself; false when the server sorts and the app reloads on sort changes.

options.name: loading
options.description: With no rows, shows placeholder rows; with rows, adds them after the last row.

options.name: errorMessage
options.description: With no rows, shows the error state with this message.

options.name: filtered
options.description: No rows means the filters matched nothing: the filtered empty state.

options.name: rowLabel
options.description: A row's name in the list layout and in spoken labels. By default the first shown cell.

options.name: rowSelectable
options.description: Whether a row has a checkbox.

options.name: rowActions
options.description: A row's actions: an actions menu and the same actions as TalkBack actions.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Adds a retry button to the error state.

options.name: onClearFilters
options.description: Adds Clear filters to the filtered empty state.

options.name: onOpen
options.description: Makes each row a button that opens the record; its name is in the link color.

options.name: actionsIcon
options.description: The actions button's icon. Without it the button shows "Actions".

options.name: state
options.description: The scroll state of the rows.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings.

options.name: footer
options.description: Content after the last row, such as a MonarchLoadMore for paged data.

states.name: table
states.description: A header row with sortable headers (a mark after the sorted one), then a row per record with a cell per shown column, a checkbox column and an actions column when used.

states.name: list
states.description: One record per row: checkbox, the name in bold (link-coloured when it opens), a field name and value per other column, and an actions button; a Sort button sits above the rows.

states.name: selected
states.description: Checked checkboxes on the accent's subtle fill, and "3 selected" beside Select all rows.

states.name: loading
states.description: With no rows, skeleton rows named "Loading rows"; with rows, skeleton rows after the last one.

states.name: failed
states.description: With no rows, a MonarchErrorState, "These rows could not be loaded", with the message and a retry button.

states.name: filtered
states.description: A filtered MonarchEmptyState, "No rows match these filters", with Clear filters.

appearance: Rows on the surface fill with a 1dp subtle divider; selected rows on the accent's subtle fill. Headers and field names are muted; numeric cells are aligned to the end with tabular figures; an empty cell shows a muted dash. Danger actions use the danger text color. Every color is a theme role, so dark and both high-contrast themes follow the theme.
platformNotes: Compose has no data table, so Monarch draws one on a LazyColumn; the table layout gives each column at least 128dp and scrolls sideways when the columns need more than the screen, so a phone shows the first columns and the rest are a swipe away; a MonarchColumnChooser can hide columns to fit. Cells are text from each column's value; the web's custom cell renderers, expandable rows, column resizing, multi-column sort, keyboard grid navigation, pagination, density and select-all-matching are not offered (use footer with a MonarchLoadMore for paging). Sorting, selection, hidden columns and the order are hoisted, as on iOS; iOS can also keep the sort internally. Row actions are a menu and TalkBack actions; iOS adds swipe actions, which Android leaves to the app (see the row-actions-menu recipe). The automatic layout switches at 640dp, the breakpoint the web uses, rather than iOS's size classes. The sort marks and the empty-cell dash are built-in resources that are not read by TalkBack and have no override.
accessibility: The table is a traversal group named by caption.
In the list layout each record is one element read as its name and "Field, value" for each column, with "No value" for an empty cell; with onOpen it is a button with the action "Open details".
Row actions are TalkBack actions on the row, and also a separate button named "Actions for" and the row's name with a 48dp touch target.
Each checkbox is named "Select" and the row's name; Select all rows is a tri-state checkbox read with the selected count.
Sortable headers are headings and buttons with the state "Sorted ascending", "Sorted descending" or "Not sorted"; the list layout's Sort button reads the sorted column and direction as its state.
Loading rows are one element named "Loading rows" with an indeterminate progress.
At font scale 1.5 and above the automatic layout is the list, and record text wraps.
edgeCases: Empty cells sort last in both directions; numeric columns sort by the number in the text, ignoring grouping marks and currency.
A sort on an unknown or unsortable column leaves the rows in the app's order.
rowKey values must be unique and savable in a Bundle; the same key twice breaks the lazy list.
The select-all checkbox selects only rows that rowSelectable allows and keeps other selected keys.
With rowLabel the list layout shows every shown column under the name; without it the first column is the name.

examples.title: Sorting, selection, row actions and grid keyboard
examples.webExample: Sorting, selection, row actions and grid keyboard
examples.template:
MonarchDataTable(
    caption = {{caption}},
    rows = invoices,
    columns = columns,
    rowKey = { it.id },
    layout = MonarchDataTableLayout.Table,
    sort = sort,
    onSortChange = { sort = it },
    selection = selected,
    onSelectionChange = { selected = it },
    rowActions = {
        listOf(
            MonarchDataTableRowAction({{rowActions.0}}) {},
            MonarchDataTableRowAction({{rowActions.1}}, danger = true) {},
        )
    },
    onOpen = {},
)
examples.code:
MonarchDataTable(

    rows = invoices,

    layout = MonarchDataTableLayout.Table,

    onSortChange = { sort = it },
    selection = selected,
    onSelectionChange = { selected = it },
    rowActions = {
        listOf(
            MonarchDataTableRowAction("Send reminder") {},
            MonarchDataTableRowAction("Void invoice", danger = true) {},
        )
    },
    onOpen = {},
)

    caption = "Invoices",

    rowKey = { it },
    filtered = true,
    onClearFilters = {},
)

parityExceptions.reason: The web table shows Customer, Status, Issued, Owner and Amount side by side in about 620px. A phone window of 392dp leaves 344dp, and the selection and actions columns take 96dp of it, so five columns at a readable 112dp each (no mid-word breaks) need about 650dp. The table therefore scrolls sideways, starting at the same columns and in the same order as the web.
parityExceptions.convention: Material data tables scroll horizontally on a compact window rather than shrink columns below a readable width
